profile.headline: Software Engineer at Microsoft
profile.summary:
Programmers are wizards.

Or so I thought when I imagined software engineering as a career. And seeing that I didn't get an invitation to Hogwarts, I didn't know if I had enough magic to make it into the not-so-secret society of coding wizards.

But after getting accepted into a little magic boot camp, Ada Developer's Academy, and learning the ways of wizards and witches, it turns out I had more magic than I thought I did. And now I'm a proud member of the not-so-secret society of coding wizards.

But I'm still very much a student. With so many languages and technologies and fields, being a software engineer feels like drinking from a goblet of knowledge that's constantly refilling itself. And that's what I really love about software engineering, there's just so much to learn.

So far, I've had the honor to work in both web frontend and web backend for about two years each. I'd like to continue my journey expanding my knowledge in other fields of software engineering, including but not limited to: infrastructure, networking, big data, reliability, desktop applications, etc.

What I value?
	- customer-focused: whether it be boosting performance, increasing usability, or implementing a desired feature, a company is nothing without its customers
	- communication: people who are willing to communicate and knowing what and who to communicate information to, and doing so in a concise and timely manner
	- respect and trust: respect from both team leads and colleagues, knowing mistakes happen and that nobody is perfect, treating each other as intelligent and well-meaning, having the trust to respectfully speak up and in turn be heard

What am I looking for?
	- continued learning: opportunities to learn new technologies and languages, but also new concepts and structures
	- mentorship: both people who are willing to help out with continued learning and career growth, but also the opportunity to help out more junior engineers
	- work-life balance: life happens, there's no escaping it, and sometimes you need the occasional work-from-home day or flexible hours; not to say there can't be the occasional crunch time or on-call, but being respectful of people's lives is all I ask

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Software engineer in Xbox social services.

positions.title: Software Development Engineer II (Web Backend)
positions.description:
• Collaborated across multiple teams to help design, implement, and deliver the first on-demand IBM i virtual machines (VMs) in the cloud, allowing enterprises to move legacy IBM i applications into the cloud. Wrote script and API endpoints to apply IBM i software licenses to customer VMs and developed report for billing customers.
• Automated security reporting for Brakeman and Bundler-Audit for Ruby on Rails code using Jenkins pipeline, as well as fixed high-risk security concerns.
• Develop REST APIs primarily in Ruby on Rails, which are consumed both internally by the frontend team and externally by Skytap customers.
• Other responsibilities include: writing documentation and keeping said documentation up-to-date, reviewing design documents, assisting with interview loops, mentoring new hires, code reviewing, fixing bugs, writing unit and integration tests, and reducing tech debt by refactoring existing code or removing unused code.

positions.title: Software Development Engineer (Web Frontend)
positions.description:
• Worked closely with two other engineers to develop from the ground up an application to help import VMs on a large scale into Skytap, implementing a React UI powered by a GraphQL API using Apollo and SQLite.
• Collaborated with backend engineers, UX, and PMs to successfully release multiple features, including privacy and consent page, which was done on a tight schedule in order to be GDPR compliant within a month.
• Converted both legacy Ruby on Rails UI pages and legacy Backbone.js UI pages to use React and Redux, increasing maintainability and user-experience consistency.
• Drove adoption of the BEM methodology for CSS and HTML, implementing style guides and documentation, opportunistically converting existing CSS to follow BEM, which increased speed at which the fellow developers could write CSS and making CSS easier to reuse and edit in the future.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description:
• Delivered multiple frontend features to improve user experience for company that sells on-demand, cloud environments.
• Converted legacy Mocha.js integration tests to Cucumber tests.
• Modernized legacy Ruby on Rails UI page using Backbone.js, CoffeeScript, Jade/Pug, and Sass.

positions.title: Student Software Developer
positions.description:
• Building skills and gaining experiences necessary to be a full-stack developer through a year-long, intensive program both in-the-classroom and in an internship.
• Completed Ruby, Rails, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS projects every 1 to 2 weeks, totaling over 20+ projects.
• Focused on object-oriented programming and test driven development.
• Collaborated in pairs and in four-person groups using Git and GitHub.

positions.title: Office Manager
positions.description:
• Maintain Intuit QuickBooks company file: record sales orders, invoices, and received payments; pay incoming bills; reconcile against bank statements; keep inventory, vendor, and customer databases up to date.
• Troubleshoot computer, printer, and network problems.
• Sort incoming mail, and write business correspondence and emails.
• Answer phone calls and take messages.
• Design forms, templates, and labels for business correspondence.
• Develop procedures and training material for an organized and efficient office.

positions.title: Game Advisor
positions.description:
• Assisted and advised customers, worked cash register, answered the phone, and helped keep store organized and clean.
• Worked during the holiday season, offering customer service and support during high volumes of customers.
